{"id":6,"jsonrpc":"2.0","result":{"content":[{"text":"{\"ok\":true,\"result\":{\"build\":\"0.1.0\",\"lookup\":\"Fetch another topic using catalog guide; repository access is unnecessary.\",\"related_topics\":[\"workflow\",\"motion\",\"graph\",\"glossary\",\"candidates\"],\"text\":\"---\\nname: fold\\ndescription: Create and edit artwork in a running Fold project through MCP or fold-cli agent. Use for motion graphics, compositing, timelines, reusable artist-editable setups, and investigating slow artwork playback; repository implementation follows the repository's development instructions.\\n---\\n\\nOperate Fold through its public tools. Use the live catalog, inspected documents, and this skill's references as the authoring contract. Routine artwork must not require reading Rust crates, editing project archives, or calling private native APIs. If the contract leaves a capability unclear, inspect a tool-created example or make a small reversible probe; report a missing capability when neither resolves it.\\n\\n## Establish the task\\n\\n1. Discover `sessions`; select the intended project by path and documents. Reuse that session throughout the exercise. Before launching a desktop, check for an existing instance; when a release launch is needed, open the requested project in one instance and rediscover it. Resolve ambiguity between matching sessions. Connections require Agent → Allow local connections, or launch with `--agent`.\\n2. Read `state`, then scope `catalog` by `method` for request schemas or `type` and `query` for package operations and nodes. Inspect existing targets with JSON pointers and pagination. Poll inspection jobs and read their nested outcome before using the data.\\n3. For a visual reference, inspect actual images and multiple animation times. Match cached media to the supplied source before using it. Establish composition, timing, and likely artist edits before construction; resolve whether visible labels, guides, and selection markers belong in the recreation. If the reference is inaccessible, obtain the missing visual evidence rather than inventing its contents.\\n\\nFor CLI access: `fold-cli agent sessions`, then `fold-cli agent call SESSION METHOD '{}'`. Pass `-` instead of JSON to read long arguments from stdin. MCP tool names have the `fold_` prefix; both transports use the same authoring contract.\\n\\n## Prove the construction\\n\\nFor unfamiliar concepts or a new procedural design, read the [authoring glossary](references/glossary.md). It distinguishes fields from uniform values, sampling domains, coordinate spaces, and reusable definitions from instances.\\n\\nFor Motion objects, text, copies, or group interfaces, read [Motion authoring](references/motion.md) before building. It supplies the coordinates, resource setup, and typed wiring conventions that node signatures alone do not explain.\\n\\nFor graph restructuring, combined node creation, control publication, graph queries, or Rust Wrangles, read [Graph authoring and Rust Wrangles](references/graph-authoring.md). Use resolved signatures and mutation receipts to avoid reconstructing node plumbing.\\n\\nFor slow playback, large instance counts, Wrangle/native performance choices, or output equivalence after optimization, read [Performance and output equivalence](references/performance.md). It separates artwork checks through MCP from engineering profiling and defines the evidence needed for a speed claim.\\n\\nBuild the smallest useful part first: one visible source, its placement, and one driver or published control. Render it before multiplying copies or assembling a large graph. A successful validation proves structure, not appearance or editability. Before finalizing an instance-heavy effect, repeat the render check at its intended count and resolution; the small probe does not establish production throughput.\\n\\nDesign around the artist's next edit. Keep content, distribution, and drivers independently editable; reuse sources across copies. Prefer shipped tools and editable groups. Name scene objects and expose useful controls with units, sections, and sensible defaults. Keep internals inside groups and distinguish whole-object from per-copy changes. Make referenced sources reachable from the artist-facing controls, including hidden text/shape targets. Put key moments on the layer's native animation track. Change instance inputs for local revisions; edit shared definitions only when all instances should change.\\n\\n## Commit against observed state\\n\\nDiscover `candidate` and `observe` through `catalog` before relying on them; older running builds may lack these methods. When available, follow [candidate authoring and observation](references/candidates.md): stage privately, render and inspect the exact generation, then commit once. This guide is also available through `catalog` with `guide: \\\"candidates\\\"`; `guide: \\\"workflow\\\"`, `\\\"motion\\\"`, `\\\"graph\\\"`, and `\\\"glossary\\\"` retrieve the other shipped essentials without repository access. `sdk: true` retrieves the client-side JavaScript authoring prototype and TypeScript declarations.\\n\\nOn older builds, submit related edits in one labeled `batch`, using the observed `revision` and `project_epoch`. Allocate identities through `ids` and `{\\\"$ref\\\":\\\"name\\\"}`; artwork strings remain literal. Prefer targeted property and connection operations, preserving user animation, disconnected work, unknown data, and world placement.\\n\\nEvery distinct proposal gets a new `request_id`, including committing a previously validated proposal. Reuse an ID only for an identical retry after a lost response. Poll `jobs` until completion and inspect `outcome.ok`; acceptance is not commitment. Consume results promptly because retention is bounded.\\n\\nOn a conflict, refresh state **and affected content**, reconcile the user's changes, then propose a new batch. Refresh IDs after project replacement or reopening. During an active user edit, continue independent reads and retry once it finishes. Global undo may include user work: check the current revision and undo label first. Cancellation cannot reverse committed work.\\n\\n## Verify and hand back\\n\\n- Render representative times and animation boundaries. For loops, sample intermediate motion and both sides of wrap boundaries at the same revision and dimensions. Output times are half-open: the duration endpoint is invalid. If the document contains multiple periods, compare matching phases inside the valid range. Equal frames alone do not establish movement. Exact rational times avoid rounding drift.\\n- Exercise likely control edits in an isolated copy when practical, then remove test work. Otherwise distinguish rendered behavior from untested control interactions.\\n- Use `viewers` and `capture` to inspect the displayed result; check identities and stale status. Captures exclude chrome, overlays, and window zoom. `navigate` deliberately changes the named viewer and stops its playback. Use portal `screenshot` when the actual interface needs review.\\n- MCP `jobs` returns images directly; CLI image results contain PNG base64 to decode and view. Report rendering/runtime failures as errors, not black artwork. Keep environment repair separate from creative edits; use documented installation guidance instead of reconstructing runtime internals.\\n- Save to the requested or agreed destination with a fresh revision guard and verify the save outcome. Saving can change `project_epoch`; refresh state afterward. When reopening is requested, reopen the saved file, rediscover the session, inspect retained controls/resources, and render it again before claiming completion. {"id":7,"jsonrpc":"2.0","result":{"content":[{"text":"{\"ok\":true,\"result\":{\"build\":\"0.1.0\",\"lookup\":\"Fetch another topic using catalog guide; repository access is unnecessary.\",\"related_topics\":[\"workflow\",\"motion\",\"graph\",\"glossary\",\"candidates\"],\"text\":\"# Candidate authoring and observation\\n\\nUse when making an experimental edit, constructing an effect, or inspecting animation without changing artist playback. Discover the actual running build with `catalog` first. CLI method names below have an MCP `fold_` prefix. Every asynchronous operation is complete only after `jobs` returns `status: \\\"complete\\\"` and `outcome.ok: true`.\\n\\n1. Read `state`. Record `revision` and `project_epoch`; identify the intended documents. Read the relevant package `catalog` and configured signatures before wiring unfamiliar nodes.\\n2. Call `candidate` with `action: \\\"begin\\\"`, a fresh `request_id`, the observed `revision`, and `project_epoch`. Record the returned candidate ID, generation, candidate revision, and base revision. The live project is unchanged.\\n3. Call `candidate` with `action: \\\"edit\\\"`, a fresh outer `request_id`, `candidate`, `generation`, `project_epoch`, and `batch`. The nested batch uses the candidate's current revision and epoch, ordinary operations/IDs, its own request ID and label, and `validate_only: false`. Poll the job. Success returns the next generation, candidate revision, allocated IDs and receipts. A failed edit leaves the previous generation intact. Use returned literal IDs in later batches.\\n4. Call `inspect`, `render`, or `observe` with `candidate`, the exact `generation`, and `project_epoch`. `inspect` supports the package query and JSON pointers. Candidate inspection cannot use `since_revision`. `observe` samples 1–12 exact times and returns one row-major strip, rectangles/timestamps and package measurements. Poll and inspect the result before proposing corrections. Evidence from an earlier generation describes earlier artwork.\\n5. Repeat private edits if necessary, always using the last successful candidate revision and generation. `state.candidates` lists retained generations. New observations do not move playback or alter the viewer.\\n6. Commit with `action: \\\"commit\\\"`, a fresh `request_id`, `candidate`, `generation`, `project_epoch`, `revision` equal to the original base revision, and a meaningful `label`. Success creates one undo action. A live revision conflict requires observing the artist's changes and rebuilding; there is no automatic rebase. Discard unwanted work with `action: \\\"discard\\\"`, request ID, candidate, generation and epoch.\\n7. Save the committed project through the ordinary revision-guarded `save` method. Read state afterward because saving may change the epoch. Verify persistence before claiming save/reopen success.\\n\\n## Observation request\\n\\nUse actual document/candidate identities from your session. This shape is exercised by `scripts/check_agent_candidates.py` and the public socket integration test:\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\"source\\\": {\\\"document\\\": \\\"DOCUMENT_UUID\\\", \\\"output\\\": \\\"video\\\"},\\n  \\\"times\\\": [{\\\"numerator\\\": 0, \\\"denominator\\\": 1}, {\\\"numerator\\\": 1, \\\"denominator\\\": 2}],\\n  \\\"dimensions\\\": [160, 90],\\n  \\\"candidate\\\": 1,\\n  \\\"generation\\\": 1,\\n  \\\"project_epoch\\\": 0,\\n  \\\"queries\\\": [{\\\"mode\\\": \\\"evaluated\\\", \\\"fields\\\": [\\\"counts\\\", \\\"elements\\\"], \\\"limit\\\": 32}]\\n}\\n```\\n\\nTimes must be within the output's half-open range. Total requested pixels cannot exceed 2,000,000; each frame is at most 2048×2048. Larger dimensions supply more detail without thumbnail resampling. At most eight queries run per time; `observe` supplies query time. Omit candidate identity to inspect the pinned committed root.\\n\\nMotion's evaluated query defaults to the scene. Set `object` to a scene object ID, or `node` plus `output` to a graph socket. `object` and `node` are exclusive. Object queries evaluate its construction independently of direct-render visibility. `counts` reports recursive geometry and top-level domain counts; `elements` reports bounded document-space transforms, opacity, shaped advances and glyph clusters. `bounds` reports analytic outline/point bounds, excluding stroke, effects and clipping. A nested-glyph diagnostic explains when a top-level glyph consumer would match nothing. Field outputs with no uniform sample are inconclusive. Image evidence remains necessary for masks, clipping, readability and visible pixels. Unsupported measurements return explicit errors/unavailable results.\\n\\n## Native SDK authoring\\n\\nFetch `catalog` with `sdk: true` for the JavaScript module, fluent TypeScript declarations, and generated operation declarations. Call `author` with candidate, generation, epoch, a fresh request ID, label, optional returned IDs as `handles`, and a JavaScript `source` body. Fold supplies `plan` and `expr` and executes the body in a bounded runtime. For example, the source body can be:\\n\\n```js\\nplan.document('title')\\n  .info({width: 320, height: 180, frames: 192, rate: [24, 1]})\\n  .object('label', 'fold.motion.text', 'Title')\\n  .set('text', 'i love katie')\\n  .set('size', 24);\\n```\\n\\nPoll the author job; success returns IDs and the new candidate generation. Store the returned `ids` as `handles` on the next author request; repeated named declarations then target existing native identities instead of duplicating content. Pass literal existing UUIDs to `existingDocument`/`existingNode` for inspected artwork. `set`, `connect`, and `settings` update only targeted properties; unmentioned artist edits survive. `Document.edit` and `FoldPlan.operation` accept the same package and transaction operations advertised by catalog. Inspect an existing handle before reuse. The low-level operation declarations are generated from package-owned Rust types; generic JSON patches still require the configured signature and catalog. Client-side code can also import the module, construct `FoldPlan`, and submit `plan.batch()` through candidate edit. Execution limits: 64 KiB source, 32 MiB heap, two seconds, 1 MiB emitted batch; no filesystem, process or network APIs. Use explicit package import operations for resources.\\n\\n## Retention and recovery\\n\\nAt most four candidates remain for 15 idle minutes. Each has a 4096-mutation and 64 MiB document-payload budget (including retained mutation payloads). Disconnecting the local agent server clears candidates; a transport reconnect alone retains the session. Project epoch changes expire candidates. Poll accepted jobs promptly; job and retry records have separate bounded retention. An identical request ID retries the original result; use a fresh ID for a revised proposal. Cancellation before candidate publication preserves its prior generation. Already committed work requires a revision-checked undo.\\n\\n## Native expressions and sampled checks\\n\\n`Document.expression(key, expression, inputs)` creates an inspectable native field. `expr.time`, `expr.input(name)`, `expr.value(value)`, `expr.binary(operation,a,b)`, and `expr.vector(x,y)` construct typed expressions. Inputs declare tagged defaults (for example `{speed:{Scalar:-50}}`); connect controls to these named inputs. Numeric binary operands must have identical types. Use `object.role('transform',{translation:driver.link()})` for a whole phrase. Configure domain-specific response nodes for individual glyphs/copies after checking evaluated domain counts.\\n\\nFor geometric checks use `inspect` with `query:{mode:'verify',check:'direction',target:{object:objectId},times:[{numerator:0,denominator:1},{numerator:1,denominator:1}],expected:[-1,0],tolerance:0.01}`. Supported checks are movement, direction, displacement, periodicity and nonempty. These return sampled native geometry and explicit limitations; use rendered observations for visibility and aesthetics. Periodicity requires endpoints plus an intermediate sample; pair it with movement to reject static output. `inspect` can evaluate the mathematical endpoint; render/observe/export use the half-open output range.\\n\",\"topic\":\"candidates\"}}","type":"text"}],"isError":false}}

{"id":9,"jsonrpc":"2.0","result":{"content":[{"text":"{\"ok\":true,\"result\":{\"build\":\"0.1.0\",\"lookup\":\"Fetch another topic using catalog guide; repository access is unnecessary.\",\"related_topics\":[\"workflow\",\"motion\",\"graph\",\"glossary\",\"candidates\"],\"text\":\"# Motion authoring through the public tools\\n\\nUse `catalog(type=\\\"fold.motion.document\\\", query=...)` for current sockets and settings. The conventions below were exercised through live MCP authoring and rendering. Resolve differences with the running catalog and a small rendered probe; these examples are not a substitute for discovery.\\n\\n## Sources and coordinates\\n\\n| Task | Construction and check |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| Visible source | `object` creates a scene object and its appearance/transform nodes. Use batch edit receipts for the created source/appearance/transform IDs; inspect the relevant graph neighborhood for existing objects. `add` creates only a graph node; it needs an output path to become visible. |\\n| Rectangle placement | A raw rectangle spans `(0,0)` to `(width,height)`. To use a centered unit cell, transform a 1×1 rectangle by `[-0.5,-0.5]` **before** copying and scaling it. Pixel coordinates increase right and down. |\\n| Text resource | Create text with `object`, which embeds a font and sets `settings.font`. A raw `add` text node defaults to `font: null` and cannot render. Inspection exposes font IDs/names, not resource bytes. Keep the embedded font in the document. |\\n| Text alignment | Text `alignment` is 0 left, 0.5 center, 1 right. This aligns horizontal advance; it does not vertically center visible glyphs. Render and adjust a source transform for the chosen font/text. A fixed vertical offset is not an automatic fit for arbitrary multiline text. |\\n| Color | Author in the project's working color space and inspect the rendered display transform. Display RGB/hex values are not automatically working-space values. Check whites and thin lines at the actual preview size; large scene-linear values can wash out antialiased boundaries after display conversion. |\\n\\nFor a simple reusable source, `extract` retains the node ID as a group instance. Inspect its `settings.group` and generated definition before modifying ports; the existing cross-feature script demonstrates this with a scalar driver.\\n\\nWhen adding text inside a group, reuse an inspected embedded font ID from the **same document**. If none exists, create a text object to establish the resource, inspect its font and generated scene nodes, and connect or incorporate that source into the intended construction. Remove a temporary helper only after its replacement renders; preserve unrelated scene objects and nodes. Avoid leaving a setup label visible over the final artwork.\\n\\n## Typed edits, not ambiguous merges\\n\\nWithin a batch's `edit` operation, these operations address a node in the main graph. Add `\\\"group\\\":\\\"GROUP_UUID\\\"` to address a group's internal graph.\\n\\n```json\\n[\\n  {\\\"op\\\":\\\"set\\\",\\\"node\\\":\\\"NODE_UUID\\\",\\\"input\\\":\\\"text\\\",\\\"value\\\":{\\\"Text\\\":\\\"FOLD\\\"}},\\n  {\\\"op\\\":\\\"connect\\\",\\\"node\\\":\\\"NODE_UUID\\\",\\\"input\\\":\\\"size\\\",\\n   \\\"source\\\":{\\\"node\\\":\\\"DRIVER_UUID\\\",\\\"socket\\\":\\\"value\\\"}},\\n  {\\\"op\\\":\\\"node\\\",\\\"node\\\":\\\"MATH_UUID\\\",\\\"value\\\":{\\\"settings\\\":{\\\"operation\\\":\\\"Multiply\\\"}}}\\n]\\n```\\n\\n`set` writes a literal; `connect` installs a link. They replace the socket's prior input. Inspected graph inputs serialize as `{\\\"Value\\\":{\\\"Scalar\\\":64}}` or `{\\\"Link\\\":{\\\"node\\\":\\\"UUID\\\",\\\"socket\\\":\\\"value\\\"}}`. These are mutually exclusive variants. A `node` merge that adds `Link` over an existing `Value` can leave both tags and fail decoding. Use the dedicated operations to change input modes. `disconnect` removes the input; follow with a literal when that socket needs a value.\\n\\nMath and Mix use Scalar signatures unless `settings.value_type` selects Vector or Color. Math operands must have identical types; combine two scalar channels when scaling a vector by a scalar. Mix weight is Scalar, while Compare outputs Bool: use selection sockets for comparisons or a scalar Map Range for blend weights. Color Ramp interpolation uses `Linear`, `Smooth`, or `Stepped`.\\n\\nFor new raw nodes in group definitions, use `version: 1`, declared defaults from the catalog, `settings`, and a two-number `position`. Required sockets without defaults need connections. Each input contains exactly one `Value` or `Link` variant.\\n\\n## Editable group interfaces\\n\\nPrefer adapting an inspected or extracted group over inventing its schema. A group definition contains `name`, `version`, `inputs`, `outputs`, and `graph`. Its graph has `nodes` and one `output` link. Public outputs point to explicit `group_output` nodes, whose `value_type` matches the exported content.\\n\\nA port is a stable key plus artist-facing metadata:\\n\\n```json\\n{\\\"id\\\":\\\"label\\\",\\\"name\\\":\\\"Text\\\",\\\"kind\\\":\\\"Text\\\",\\\"default\\\":{\\\"Text\\\":\\\"FOLD\\\"},\\n \\\"unit\\\":\\\"\\\",\\\"section\\\":\\\"Text\\\",\\\"advanced\\\":false}\\n```\\n\\nThe corresponding internal `group_input` has `settings: {\\\"key\\\":\\\"label\\\",\\\"value_type\\\":\\\"Text\\\"}` and a `value` output. Connect it to the text node's `text` socket. Its `Generic` catalog socket does not mean arbitrary types are interchangeable: the port kind, default datum, and settings must agree. Use a typed Text group port for a text field; the standalone Published Control node is not a replacement for all group port types.\\n\\nFor a content output, an internal `group_output` has `settings: {\\\"value_type\\\":\\\"Content\\\"}` and a `value` input linked to the final content. The definition exports it as:\\n\\n```json\\n{\\\"outputs\\\":{\\\"content\\\":{\\\"node\\\":\\\"OUTPUT_UUID\\\",\\\"socket\\\":\\\"value\\\"}}}\\n```\\n\\nAn outer `group_instance` has `settings.group` set to the definition ID. Set its inputs by stable port key, e.g. `set(node=INSTANCE, input=\\\"label\\\", value={\\\"Text\\\":\\\"MOVE\\\"})`. The definition provides defaults; the instance provides local overrides. Publishing a control requires the port **and its wiring**. Verify a changed value reaches the intended copies.\\n\\nExtend existing definitions with `add`, `set`, and `connect` scoped by `group`. Use `publish` to create a port and its wiring, and `port` for targeted metadata edits (see [graph authoring](graph-authoring.md)). For unsupported interface migrations, port arrays need a freshly inspected complete list with existing entries retained. Whole graph/scene array replacement is a last resort: merge with the observed contents and guard that exact revision. Preserve node IDs, animation, layout, and extension data rather than rebuilding the user's construction.\\n\\nWhen replacing an extracted definition's interface, disconnect obsolete overrides on the outer instance in the same batch. An instance retaining an input removed from the definition fails validation.\\n\\n## Copies and deformation\\n\\nContent → distribution → copies → response is the reusable pattern:\\n\\n1. Establish a source's local origin and appearance.\\n2. Generate points and connect the source to `instance_on_points`.\\n3. Apply per-copy `set_scale`, `set_position`, color, or opacity fields using the intended domain and combine mode from the catalog.\\n4. Share field nodes between content that must stay aligned. Share the point order too: index-based selection only matches across identical distributions.\\n\\nUse `set_position` with `combine: \\\"Replace\\\"` for absolute cell centers. Normalize the source before the copy transforms; changing size around an unintended origin creates moving gaps and offsets. Verify one source and a few copies before scaling the distribution up.\\n\\nFor live numeric labels, use `format_text` with `{value}`, `{x}`, or `{y}` and integer `decimals` from 0 to 6. `text_on_points` consumes this Text field at each selected point; ordinary Text expects a uniform string. Drive label points from the same position field as the artwork, reuse its point order/selection, and supply an embedded font ID from the same document. Position fields sample the point's upstream coordinates; include any later authored center offset when the label should report composition coordinates.\\n\\nShape Grid with `circular: true` and `world_aligned: true` samples live filled geometry after upstream transforms on a shared lattice. Use `cell_size` for spacing and `cell_scale` for dot diameter relative to spacing. This differs from copying a fixed dot patch onto each object. For outline-only marker rectangles, apply a transparent Fill before Stroke; a raw stroked rectangle otherwise retains its default fill.\\n\\n## Example: animated grid with cell text\\n\\nThis is a construction pattern, not a command to add a grid to every task. A reference clip used 11 columns, 10 rows, a two-cell white diagonal, and a one-second loop; the artist later changed counts and added text through the same setup.\\n\\nFor row `r` of `R`, total height `H`, integer wave count `k`, loop period `T`, phase `p`, and strength `s`, define a shared row boundary:\\n\\n```text\\ntheta = t / T + p\\nedge(r) = r * H/R + s * H/R *\\n          (sin(2*pi*(theta - r*k/R)) - sin(2*pi*theta))\\nheight(r) = edge(r+1) - edge(r)\\ncenter_y(r) = top + (edge(r+1) + edge(r))/2\\n```\\n\\nInteger `k` anchors both outer edges. Positive counts and period are required; keeping `0 <= s < 0.5` keeps heights positive in this model. Implement with catalog Math, Time, and Wave nodes; do not precompute animation frames. Derive row and column from the common copy index. A comparison of `abs(column-row-0.5)` against half the band width selects the white cells.\\n\\nNormalize a rectangle, then drive copies with cell width/height and center fields. Add grid outlines with consistent pixel widths. Expose the useful count, timing, strength, diagonal, and color controls on the outer instance.\\n\\nFor cell text, publish a Text port, size factor, and color. Center and normalize the embedded-font text source, copy it onto the **same points**, and reuse the rectangle's size and center fields. Hide all text copies with opacity 0, then set opacity 1 for the same white-cell selection. This makes glyphs stretch with each row while staying attached to their cells.\\n\\nThis construction repeats the whole label in each selected cell. It does not distribute letters across cells or automatically fit arbitrary strings. Render the requested text; provide a size control and check long/multiline edits if those are part of the brief. Compare compressed and expanded rows, red-cell exclusion, a changed label, and a full loop boundary. Keep the artist's later control changes when extending the setup.\\n\",\"topic\":\"motion\"}}","type":"text"}],"isError":false}}

{"id":18,"jsonrpc":"2.0","result":{"content":[{"text":"{\"ok\":true,\"result\":{\"build\":\"0.1.0\",\"lookup\":\"Fetch another topic using catalog guide; repository access is unnecessary.\",\"related_topics\":[\"workflow\",\"motion\",\"graph\",\"glossary\",\"candidates\"],\"text\":\"# Fold authoring concepts\\n\\nRead this when planning a construction or resolving terminology. Use the live catalog for exact node IDs, sockets, defaults, settings, and current capability support.\\n\\n| Concept | Meaning and authoring consequence |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| Document / output | A Motion, Composite, or Sequence document owns editable work. A document/output reference lets another document consume its result without rendering an intermediate file. Resolve both ID and output name. |\\n| Scene object / graph node | An object participates in the Motion scene. A raw node computes something; it needs a path to an authored output to become visible. `object` can establish scene wiring and resources that `add` alone does not. |\\n| Content / points | Content carries drawable geometry and hierarchy. Points describe a distribution used by consumers such as Instance on Points and Text on Points. Reuse the same distribution and ordering when overlays must correspond to copies. |\\n| Uniform value / field | A uniform value is shared; a field is sampled by its consumer using context such as position, index, identity, and count. Linking a field does not bake one value per frame. The consumer determines where sampling occurs. |\\n| Index / identity | Index is an element's position in an ordered domain; identity identifies the element. An even-index selection stays aligned only while branches retain the same ordering. Changing count can legitimately rearrange an index-derived pattern. |\\n| Domain | Which elements receive a response: for example Points or Instances. Moving label points uses Points; modifying copied circles uses Instances. Inspect supported domains instead of assuming all responses accept all domains. |\\n| Driver / influence / response | A driver produces change (Time, Wave, Keyframes); influence selects elements or supplies weights; a response applies it (position, scale, opacity). Sharing drivers preserves relationships between branches. |\\n| Selection / weight | Selection is Bool; weight is a scalar strength. A comparison cannot be wired directly to a scalar Mix weight. Use selection sockets for filtering, or a scalar mapping for blending. |\\n| Combine mode | Replace supplies an absolute value in the current space; Multiply scales an existing value. Match the mode to the intended relationship: set centers with Replace, resize existing instances with Multiply. |\\n| Local / downstream coordinates | Source geometry has an origin; later transforms change placement. Center a source before copying it. A Position field sees its consumer's upstream context, so labels need an explicit later center offset when reporting composition coordinates. |\\n| Content Group / reusable group | A Content Group combines back/front content. A reusable group defines an internal graph with typed public ports; a Group Instance references that definition. They are different operations despite the shared word. |\\n| Definition / instance override | Editing a definition changes its shared construction and defaults. Setting an instance input changes that instance. Discover its `settings.group`, inspect the definition's ports, and edit by stable port key. |\\n| Published control | A typed public port plus internal wiring. Its display name can change while its stable key stays the same. A listed control is only useful if changing it affects the intended output. |\\n| Embedded font | A resource belonging to the document. A raw text node with no font cannot render. Reuse an inspected same-document font or create a text object through public authoring to establish one. |\\n| Working / display color | Authored color values are interpreted in the working space, then transformed for display. Values above 1 may be intentional. A screenshot's RGB triplet is not automatically a valid working-space match. |\\n| Exact time | Use rational seconds, e.g. frame 45 at 30 fps is `{\\\"numerator\\\":45,\\\"denominator\\\":30}`. A period, document duration, and drift speed are separate controls unless explicitly wired together. |\\n| Viewer / delivery output | A viewer presents a selected document/output at its own time. Navigation does not establish the project's delivery choice. Displayed and requested identities can differ while a frame is pending. |\\n| Revision / project epoch | Revision guards authored state; epoch also detects project replacement/save context changes. Refresh both from `state` before mutations and after save/reopen. |\\n| Job / committed result | A returned job ID acknowledges queued work. Poll `jobs` and inspect `outcome.ok` before using inspection data, claiming an edit, or reporting a save. |\\n\\nTo plan new work, name its content, distribution, driver, influence, and response; then identify which relationships must remain shared when the artist changes a control. The [Motion reference](motion.md) provides typed wiring conventions, and the [dot-study workflow](procedural-dot-study.md) combines them into a complete construction.\\n\",\"topic\":\"glossary\"}}","type":"text"}],"isError":false}}
